Subject: DPA redline - telemetry / product improvement clause

Sergio,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our proposed DPA redline (v3) — we added a narrow carveout that would allow Redwood to use anonymized telemetry and model output metadata for product improvement and safety monitoring. The exact language is in section 4.2 (highlighted).

If you can confirm by EOD Thursday (10/8) we can proceed to legal review.

Attachments: NorthHarbor_DPA_redline_v3.pdf, telemetry_scope_table.xlsx

Thanks,

Subject: Fwd: DPA redline - telemetry / product improvement clause

Team — forwarding the redline from North Harbor. Short summary: they want a narrow clause permitting use of aggregated/anonymized telemetry + model output metadata for product improvement and safety. Legal flagged this as a potential data-use carveout that will need Product and Security sign-off before they can accept.

Specific asks:
- Product (Grace): confirm that the proposed scope (see telemetry_scope_table.xlsx) gives Redwood the data needed for meaningful model/product improvements and whether any additional constraints would break planned feedback loops.
- Security (Dev): confirm the suggested safeguards are adequate (we currently have KMS, audit logs, and role-based access) and whether we need to propose extra technical controls (e.g., differential privacy, additional logging retention limits).
- Kimberly/Legal: please advise if we should propose alternate language or a proof-of-concept clause with time-boxed scope.

Target: align internally by Thu 10/8 so I can reply to James and push to their legal.

Forwarded attachments: NorthHarbor_DPA_redline_v3.pdf, telemetry_scope_table.xlsx

-- Sergio

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline - telemetry / product improvement clause

Thanks for the ping, Sergio — reviewed the scope table. Quick notes from Product: 

- The narrow telemetry fields they list (API call metadata, model output confidence scores, coarse usage buckets) are generally sufficient for iterative model improvements and monitoring. We would NOT need raw user messages.
- Retention: 30 days rolling for raw telemetry; aggregated metrics can be kept longer (90 days) for trend analysis. If Legal requires stricter retention, we can usually operate with 14 days raw + 60 days aggregated but it will slow our regression detection.
- Versioning: please add a pinning requirement that any telemetry used for model training/weight updates must reference a specific model version and be subject to the customer's opt-out for training. We should avoid open-ended training rights.

Open question: do we need to propose differential privacy or stronger de-identification? For most customers the aggregation + model-version pin is acceptable, but for high-risk verticals (finance/health) we should propose DP.

Happy to draft slightly tightened language for the carveout if Legal wants a starting point.

-Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr. PM, Model Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: James Connors <j.connors@northharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline - telemetry / product improvement clause

Appreciate the summary. Security comments below: 

- Controls: current stack (KMS for key management, TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest) meets baseline. We need to add:
  * Customer-scoped audit logging retained for 365 days and accessible for incident review upon lawful request (we can gate this to admin roles).
  * Fine-grained IAM scoping for who can access telemetry-derived artifacts (no developer-default access).
  * A short-proof requirement: show a plan for how telemetry will be de-identified before it is used for any model training pipeline (pseudonymization + metadata-only).
- Technical redlines to propose: require explicit model-version tagging and disable automated training unless the customer opt-in is present.
- If Legal accepts, Security would prefer the retention clause be explicitly time-boxed in the DPA (e.g., raw telemetry 30 days, aggregate 90 days) and that any extension requires a documented business justification with Security sign-off.

I'll work a suggested paragraph for Security to include; can have a draft by EOD Wednesday.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Platform Security
Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: James Connors <j.connors@northharbor.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline - telemetry / product improvement clause

James — thanks for the redline and patience. Quick internal alignment summary and proposed next steps: 

1) Product (Grace) confirms the scope in telemetry_scope_table.xlsx covers the signals needed. Product prefers: raw telemetry retention = 30 days, aggregated = 90 days. Product requests explicit model-version pinning and an opt-out for training.
2) Security (Dev) confirms baseline controls are acceptable but requests: customer-scoped audit log retention (365 days), fine-grained IAM for telemetry artifacts, and an explicit de-identification step before any training. Security will draft a short paragraph to insert into the DPA.
3) Legal (Kimberly) — please advise whether we should propose the Product+Security language as a time-limited pilot (90 days) or as permanent language with the retention windows above. A pilot could simplify acceptance.

Suggested next steps: I will send an internal draft paragraph (combining Product + Security asks) by COB today; Kimberly, if you can flag any absolute legal no-nos I will incorporate them before sending back to James. If North Harbor agrees to the pilot approach, we can include a proof-of-concept clause and check-in dates (90 days).

Please reply with any objections — otherwise I will circulate the draft language to the thread and to Legal Ops (NH) by EOD.

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
